For both a single-burner induction cooktop and most electric kettles, I’d choose the **[BLUETTI Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2)**. Its **2,600 W AC output** is enough for an induction burner drawing up to 1,800 W, and its **2,073.6 Wh battery** gives you useful cooking time. At full burner power, expect around an hour of continuous use after conversion losses; ordinary cooking with lower heat and pauses will last longer. ([specs and buying link](https://dealectric.com/power-station-that-can-run-an-induction-cooktop))

Check your appliance’s label before buying: the power station’s **continuous AC output** needs to meet or exceed the cooktop or kettle’s wattage. For reference, a common single-burner cooktop can draw **up to 1,800 W**. ([cooktop power guide](https://homepowerfacts.com/can-it-run/induction-cooktop/))
